correctness.rationale: The exact rectangle polynomial identity is reconstructed by multiplying the proposed U-V expression by (1-X^a)(1-X^b) and using a alpha+b beta=ab+1. Degree uniqueness and disjoint residue classes eliminate cancellation. Both residue families are partitioned into explicit integer rows, and inter-/intra-row gap counts recover every multiplicity including gap one. A separate coefficient recurrence checked 810 admissible cases and 8,050,320 coefficient positions; it is supplementary rather than an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2015 general result supplies only the maximum gap multiplicity and a qualitative all-length characterization; the 2021 word formula computes coefficients, not these closed two-parameter histogram formulas; the 2025 full-spectrum count is restricted to residues plus/minus one while its arbitrary-residue result gives the second gap only. A separately published b=a+d with a=dt+1 result covers b=a+2 when d=2 and s=1, but not the new s>=2 layers or generic minus-two family. No equivalent or dominating complete plus/minus-two spectrum was found in inspected sources and actual searches; unindexed coverage is a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of a closely related published b=a+d result was not accessible, though its explicit parameter condition covers only s=1 for d=2.
Unindexed prior work may contain equivalent ±2 formulas even if direct title and semantic searches did not identify them.
A reader may treat the new law as a specialized consequence of the existing coefficient-word representation; the value here is the parameter-uniform closed spectrum and row-geometry proof.

value.rationale: The 2015–2025 literature identifies the ±1 cases as exceptional for complete gap support and leaves the first adjacent ±2 residue families without full frequency formulas. This theorem simultaneously handles all odd a, unbounded quotients, and both signs, making exact every nonunit gap multiplicity and ruling out all odd nonunit lengths. The asymmetry (equal 2s counts on +2, extra two copies at all nonmaximal even lengths on -2) is a structural distinction not implied by knowing only the two largest gaps. It also applies to composite-generator semigroup polynomials.
